_comment: Editorial copy for the deck gallery. 'illustrated' decks ship pre-rendered art, composited into a three-card fan by cardz-win's scripts/build-deck-gallery.mjs; build.mjs refuses a slug with no art in assets/decks/manifest.json. 'drawn' decks are painted by the app at runtime with no art on disk, so they are named and described but not pictured — no invented mock-ups.

illustrated.name: Valhalla
illustrated.blurb: A Norse woodcut deck. The courts are true two-headed figures, mirrored about the card's centre rather than merely drawn twice, and the pair of Loki jokers are worth finding.

illustrated.name: Scarab
illustrated.blurb: Ancient Egypt on papyrus. Alone among the decks it wears a small gold cartouche beside each index — the rank this card pairs with to make thirteen, which is Pyramid's whole problem solved in the corner of your eye.

illustrated.name: Olympus
illustrated.blurb: Gods painted on marble, with a gold index laid over the plate. A plain decorative deck: the corners hold the rank and the suit, nothing more.

illustrated.name: Herbarium
illustrated.blurb: A pressed-botanical plate book in ink and watercolour, with the four suits as four plant families — rose, marigold, clover, thistle — on a deep botanical-green table.

illustrated.name: Filigree
illustrated.blurb: Engraved vermilion and iron-gall ink, in the classic two-colour convention, laid on an antique espresso-leather writing desk.

illustrated.name: Ornamental
illustrated.blurb: The first illustrated deck Cardz shipped — drawn as vector ornament and rasterized so that every hairline survives at card size.

illustrated.name: Deepfield
illustrated.blurb: A commissioned space deck: dark navy cards, orbital pips, celestial courts, and four colours of suit instead of the usual two.

illustrated.name: Monosolid
illustrated.blurb: Paper-cut shapes in two inks against a dark ink table. Type as image, tally pips, and courts cut down to a crown, an orb, and a blade.

drawn.name: Felt House
drawn.blurb: The house deck, drawn by the app itself. Clean, classical, and the one Cardz deals with until you choose otherwise.

drawn.name: Noir
drawn.blurb: Neo-noir neon — near-black cards in cyan and magenta, glowing two-headed courts, and a lit grid on the back.

drawn.name: Colourblind
drawn.blurb: A two-colour deck built for colour-vision deficiency: blue hearts and diamonds, black spades and clubs, so the suits never rely on red against green.
